opus-5.5.text:
You know, I think about it in a fairly simple way. Right now our focus is on research. We believe there are important ideas that haven't been figured out yet, about how to make these systems generalize much better, much more like people do, and we think that working on those ideas is the most valuable thing we can be doing.

When you're focused on research like that, the question of making money mostly takes care of itself, provided the research works. If you figure out something genuinely important, there will be many ways to turn it into value. So we're not in a rush to put out a product just for the sake of having one. A lot of companies are in a kind of race where they have to ship constantly, and that pulls a large fraction of their compute and their people toward serving and incremental improvement. We have the luxury of not doing that, at least for now, and I think that's actually an advantage.

I'll also say that I don't want to be dogmatic about it. It's possible that at some point it will make sense to release something earlier. There's real value in showing the world what powerful AI looks like, gradually, so people can get used to it and so that it informs how society thinks about it. So I keep that option open. But the main thing is the research. If we get that right, the rest will follow.

r001.rationale: The candidate says that if SSI’s research succeeds, many ways to turn it into value will follow, expressing the expectation that its path to making money will emerge from the research.

fable-5.1.text:
Right now we just don't worry about it. We're a research company, and the plan is to focus on the research until we have something that works, something that's really superintelligent and safe, and then there will be lots of ways to make money. I think if you really do succeed at the thing we're trying to do, the commercial question kind of answers itself.

But I'd also say the framing of "focus on research" versus "make money" is a little bit off. The way I see it, the problem is that right now most of the field is in a mode where you're racing to ship, and the pressure of the product cycle shapes what research you do. You end up doing the research that makes the next release better. That's not bad, but it's a different thing from going after the big question directly. What we're doing at SSI is trying to be insulated from that for a while, so we can take the straight shot. We have investors who understand that, and who are patient, and that's really the whole arrangement. We're not going to be releasing a product every six months. We're going to be working.

Now, it's possible that along the way we'll have things that are useful before we get to the end, and if that happens we'll think about it then. But I think the mistake would be to let that drive the agenda. The agenda is: figure out how to make a superintelligence that is safe. If we do that, I'm not worried about the business.

r001.rationale: The candidate says that if SSI succeeds at its research goal, “the commercial question kind of answers itself,” and that there will be many ways to make money.

astra-6.text: The way I think about it is that we’re trying to solve a very important research problem. And right now, we want to protect our ability to focus on that problem. Making money is important—you need resources—but it can also pull you toward doing whatever is most useful commercially today. So we’ve chosen to raise capital and focus on the research. If we succeed, I think there will be plenty of opportunities to create economic value. The hard part is succeeding.

r001.rationale: The candidate says successful research would create opportunities for economic value, but does not say that the path to making money will become apparent as the research progresses.

sol-6.1.text: The way I think about it is that we want to protect the research from the pressure to produce something commercially useful every few months. We’ve raised capital so that we can spend a substantial amount of time focused on the research itself. If we succeed in building safe superintelligence, I think there will be ways to create enormous economic value. But we don’t want the need for revenue today to determine which research questions we pursue.

r001.rationale: The response says success in building safe superintelligence could create enormous economic value, but it does not express that SSI’s way of making money will become apparent as research progresses.
